name: Question 18
problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(3.2)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(3+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to one decimal place.
worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=3,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(3+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(3)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(3)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(3)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(3)}^{5}+5{(3)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(3)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =243+5(81)(x)+10(27)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =243+405x+270{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(3+x)}^{5}≈243+405x+270{x}^{2}
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.2$ into the above approximation of $(3+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3.2)^{5} & =(3+0.2)^{5} \\  & ≈243+405(0.2)+270(0.2)^{2} \\  & =243+405(0.2)+270(0.0\,4) \\  & =243+81+10.8 \\  & =334.8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(3.2)^{5}-334.8|}{(3.2)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.2%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

Question 18

Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of (3.2)5 using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (3+x)5 in ascending powers of x. Round your final percentage error to one decimal place.

a
0.1%
b
0.2%
c
0.4%
d
0.0%
e
0.3%
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem for positive integer n states that

(a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

By substituting a=3, b=x, and n=5, we obtain

(3+x)5=(50)(3)5(x)0+(51)(3)5−1(x)1+(52)(3)5−2(x)2+⋯=1(3)5+5(3)4(x)1+10(3)3(x)2+⋯=243+5(81)(x)+10(27)(x2)+⋯=243+405x+270x2+⋯.

So, for small x, we have

(3+x)5≈243+405x+270x2

Now, we substitute x=0.2 into the above approximation of (3+x)5:

(3.2)5=(3+0.2)5≈243+405(0.2)+270(0.2)2=243+405(0.2)+270(0.04)=243+81+10.8=334.8

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows:

%error=amount of errorexact value×100=|(3.2)5−334.8|(3.2)5×100≈0.2%

rounded to one decimal place.
